I need to add ROI (region-of-interest) cycle-measurement markers around exactly ONE matrix-vector multiply operation inside llama.cpp's ggml compute engine, at /home/nick/work/llama.cpp. This is for a RISC-V hybrid simulator project (andesim) that measures cycle-accurate performance of a single kernel operation, not a whole token generation (which would take far too long on a cycle-accurate simulator).

Context: ggml (llama.cpp's tensor library) works by building a full computation GRAPH first (calls like `ggml_mul_mat()` just add a node to the graph), then executing the WHOLE graph in one shot via something like `ggml_backend_graph_compute()`/`ggml_graph_compute`. This means individual matvec operations are NOT distinguishable at the application call-site level (e.g. in llama-model.cpp or the per-layer forward-pass code) -- they all get dispatched generically deep inside ggml's own execution loop.

I need you to find, in the CPU backend specifically (ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ -- since this target has no GPU, only CPU/RVV), the EXACT function/loop where individual graph NODES get dispatched to their compute implementation (i.e., where a `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node specifically gets routed to its actual multiply-accumulate compute function, one node at a time, during graph execution). I want to know:

1. The exact file and function name of this per-node dispatch loop (likely something like `ggml_graph_compute_thread` or a switch/dispatch on `tensor->op` in ggml-cpu.c or ggml-cpu.cpp).
2. Whether there's a clean, minimal way to insert a static counter that increments once per GGML_OP_MUL_MAT node processed, and conditionally wraps JUST the Kth occurrence's actual compute call with two marker function calls (I already have a header `<andesim/ROI.h>` providing `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()`, both are just inline asm HINT instructions with a memory clobber -- totally safe to call from anywhere, no state needed). Show me the exact current code at that insertion point (with line numbers) so I can write a minimal, precise patch.
3. Whether this dispatch loop is single-threaded when the model runs with n_threads=1 (I need to confirm there's no thread-safety concern with a plain `static int counter` at this site, given our use case always runs with -t 1).
4. For Bonsai-4B (a qwen3-architecture model, 2560 embedding dim, 36 layers, Q1_0 quantization), roughly how many GGML_OP_MUL_MAT nodes would appear in ONE token's forward-pass graph (a rough count is fine -- I want to sanity check that picking some specific K within that range, e.g. the 10th or 50th mul_mat call, would land inside one of the 36 transformer layers' attention or FFN matvecs, not in some one-off setup/embedding lookup op). If you can find where the graph gets built (per-layer loop, likely in ggml/src or the llama.cpp model-building code for qwen3) and count how many mul_mat-family ops appear per layer, that would help me pick a good K.

Do NOT modify any files -- this is pure research. Report back: the exact file:function:line for the insertion point, the exact minimal code change (as a diff-style snippet, not applied), the threading-safety answer, and the rough per-layer op count / a reasonable K to target. Keep the report focused and under 600 words plus the code snippet.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a riscv64 llama.cpp binary under Andes QEMU (user-mode).
#
# Usage:   ./run-rv64-qemu.sh <binary-name-or-path> [args...]
# Example: ./run-rv64-qemu.sh llama-bench -m model.gguf -p 8 -n 4 -r 1 -t 1
#
# Overridable via environment:
#   ANDES_ROOT  Andes SW release root
#   QEMU        Andes linux-user qemu-riscv64
#   SYSROOT     toolchain glibc sysroot (matches the xandes-built libc)
#   BIN_DIR     directory with the cross-built binaries and libggml*/libllama* .so
#   QEMU_CPU    QEMU cpu string; zfh/zvfh must be enabled explicitly:
#               andes-ax45mpv does not enable them by default and
#               ggml_cpu_fp32_to_fp16 (vfncvt.f.f.w) SIGILLs without zvfh
#   MODEL       default model, added as "-m $MODEL" when no -m is given
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ANDES_ROOT=${ANDES_ROOT:-/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542}
QEMU=${QEMU:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-qemu/linux/qemu-riscv64}
SYSROOT=${SYSROOT:-$ANDES_ROOT/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d/sysroot}
BIN_DIR=${BIN_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/build-rv64/bin}
QEMU_CPU=${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512,zfh=true,zvfh=true}

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
    echo "usage: $0 <binary-name-or-path> [args...]" >&2
    exit 1
fi

BIN=$1
shift
[ -f "$BIN" ] || BIN=$BIN_DIR/$BIN

MODEL=${MODEL:-$SCRIPT_DIR/models/Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf}
case "$(basename "$BIN")" in
    llama-cli|llama-completion|llama-bench|llama-server|llama-perplexity)
        has_model=false
        for arg in "$@"; do
            [ "$arg" = "-m" ] && has_model=true
        done
        if ! $has_model; then
            set -- "$@" -m "$MODEL"
        fi
        ;;
esac

exec "$QEMU" \
    -L "$SYSROOT" \
    -E LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$BIN_DIR" \
    -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
    "$BIN" "$@"
